answersA.text: Java 11 introduced features like local-variable type inference (var), enhanced `String` methods, and the HTTP Client API. Java 17 brought LTS features such as sealed classes, pattern matching for `instanceof`, and foreign-function memory access. Java 21, the latest LTS, includes virtual threads, structured concurrency, and pattern matching for switch. Each release builds upon the last, offering performance improvements and new language constructs.

newInput: How does caching work in Redis?

answersA.title: How caching works in Redis
answersA.text: Caching in Redis works by storing frequently accessed data in memory for fast retrieval. When a request comes in, Redis first checks its in-memory cache. If the data is found (a cache hit), it's returned immediately. If not (a cache miss), the data is fetched from the primary data store, then stored in Redis for future requests, and finally returned to the user. This significantly speeds up read operations.

answersA.title: How caching works in Redis
answersA.text: Redis can function as a cache by storing frequently accessed data in memory for fast retrieval. When a request for data comes in, the application first checks Redis. If the data is found (a cache hit), it's returned immediately. If not (a cache miss), the application fetches the data from the primary data source, stores it in Redis for future requests, and then returns it. This significantly reduces latency and load on the primary data store.

answersA.title: Redis eviction policies
answersA.text: Redis eviction policies determine which keys are removed from the cache when it reaches its memory limit. Common policies include LRU (Least Recently Used), LFU (Least Frequently Used), TTL (Time To Live), and random eviction. LRU removes the keys that haven't been accessed for the longest time. LFU removes keys that have been accessed the fewest times. TTL removes keys that have expired. Random eviction removes keys at random.
